name: element.addAttachment
title: Add attachment
summary: Copy an image, from a local file or given as bytes, into the folder named like the element file, next to it, and return the Markdown that embeds it relatively; once the text embeds it, the image counts to the version (SR-097, D-057). Never replaces a file.
whileReadOnlyReason: Adds a file to an element, and no change can be checked against a missing or faulty metamodel.

sourcePath.description: The image to copy: a file ending in .avif, .bmp, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, .svg or .webp (any case). Give it or content, not both.

content.description: The bytes of the image, base64 (RFC 4648, with padding), at most 20 MiB decoded, so a request stays below the 32 MiB limit of the API and MCP: for an image without a file, such as one pasted or dropped in the app (SR-190 AK3). Needs name; give it or sourcePath, not both.

name.description: The file name of content, for its extension (which must be one of sourcePath's) and the name of the copy, e.g. Screenshot 2026-11-07.png. Only with content.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares, SR-088; ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#255). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (ThomasBirkmaier/ReqSeq-archive#255). Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

The image file relative to the workspace root, / as separator, e.g. requirements/SR-825b7146fb54/layout.png. Its name is the source name with only ASCII letters, digits, _ and -, and -2, -3, ... when the folder has that name already; a file there with the same bytes is reused.

markdown.description: The image as Markdown with a link relative to the element file, e.g. ![layout](SR-825b7146fb54/layout.png), to insert into the text and save with element.update.
